PATHOGEN: Prion disease with a long incubation
CONTROL MEASURE: Cull of infected and contact herds

Highly contagious viral disease.requires: airborne or contact spread between herds
Highly contagious viral disease.provides: spread over kilometres without any movement of animals, no treatment, statutory notifiable status

Vector-borne viral disease.requires: a competent insect vector and a season
Vector-borne viral disease.provides: spread bounded by vector range, no direct animal-to-animal transmission, seasonal cessation

Bacterial disease treatable with antimic.provides: treatment available, production losses rather than mortality, no need to cull

Prion disease with a long incubation.provides: no live test at all, cases appearing years after exposure, no transmission between living animals

Intensive indoor unit.provides: complete records, biosecurity feasible, catastrophic loss if breached

Extensive upland grazing.provides: no possibility of housing, contact with wildlife, gathering takes days

Smallholder mixed farm.provides: informal records, animals moved to local markets, limited biosecurity knowledge

Live animal market.requires: animals from many holdings mixed briefly
Live animal market.provides: enormous contact network in one day, no ownership continuity

Movement standstill.provides: immediate halt to spread by transport, severe welfare and trade consequences

Ring vaccination around cases.requires: an effective vaccine and cold chain
Ring vaccination around cases.provides: protection of a zone within days, loss of disease-free trading status

Cull of infected and contact herds.provides: removal of the reservoir, compensation cost and public opposition

Enhanced surveillance only.requires: a testing programme and laboratory capacity
Enhanced surveillance only.provides: detection of spread, no reduction in transmission whatsoever

Contained at the index holding.provides: minimal loss, disease-free status recovered quickly

Regional epidemic.requires: spread beyond the initial zone before detection

Endemic establishment.requires: the pathogen persisting in the population
Endemic establishment.provides: permanent change to husbandry and trade

Export market closure.provides: economic loss far exceeding the animal loss
